intro: One telur dadar is about 150 kcal (estimate). Half the calories come from the egg itself, and the other half from the frying oil.

variants.name: Telur dadar with filling (vegetables or minced meat)

diet: Yes, you can. Eggs are a cheap and easy protein source. What pushes the calories up is the oil, because telur dadar soaks up oil fast. Cook it yourself with a little oil, and it's a great lauk while dieting. At a shop, share it or pick a boiled egg if available.
tips: Use a non-stick pan and just one teaspoon of oil.
Add vegetables like onion, tomato and spring onion so it's more filling.
At a shop, pick a boiled egg or telur mata over a thick telur dadar.

swap.name: 2 boiled eggs
swap.why: Same calories as one telur dadar, but double the protein. Keeps you full longer.

faq.q: What's the difference between telur dadar and a fried egg?
faq.a: Telur dadar is beaten before frying, usually with onion and chilli. Telur mata is fried straight without beating.

faq.q: How do I make a fluffy telur dadar?
faq.a: Beat the eggs well and cook on medium heat. A little water or milk helps make it softer.

faq.q: How many eggs a day can I eat?
faq.a: For most healthy people, 1 to 2 eggs a day is normal. If you have a specific health condition, check with your doctor or a dietitian.
